PLAN: Build a lean blend-oriented front end first (C3, C4, C5), inspect splits and costs, then add only high-value heavy-product branches and tune difficult columns. Step 1: evaluate four-column front end.
Root removes ethane+C3; TT deethanizes to C3 blend. B splits C4+C5 from C6+; BT separates C4 and C5 blends. Blends sacrifice ~15-20% revenue but avoid difficult pure separations and extra columns. Heavy 1741 mol/s remains for later. Starting with moderate 45-50 stages and R=B=3 to learn convergence, purity, and cost.

note: Reconfigure the existing skeleton into sharp C5 and C6-paraffin blend cuts; this should create two valuable products with only three columns.
notebook:
PLAN: First obtain saleable C5 and C6-paraffin blends with a lean three-column skeleton, then add heavy and light recovery only where marginal revenue exceeds cost. Step 2: re-cut root after C5, T after C4, and B after C6 paraffins.
Turn 1 showed arbitrary R=B=3 cuts were far too light and no products met spec. Target flows: root T=1257 (C2-C5), B=2043 (C6+); T bottoms=695 C5 blend; B tops=970 C6 paraffin blend. Root reboil raised to 4 to carry C5 overhead. Remove BT for now. Blends retain most value and avoid expensive isomer splits. Next inspect actual splits/purities before tuning or adding heavies.

note: Sharpen all three key splits aggressively; high boil-up at the root and C4/C5 column should remove the butane and pentane contamination that blocked both blend sales.
notebook:
PLAN: First obtain saleable C5 and C6-paraffin blends with a lean three-column skeleton, then add heavy and light recovery only where marginal revenue exceeds cost. Step 3: force sharp C5/C6, C4/C5 and C6-paraffin/naphthene splits.
The R=B=3 skeleton cut far too broadly: TB held 32% butane and BT was contaminated by pentane. Blend values are about $171M/yr (C5) and $328M/yr (C6 paraffins), enough to beat a ~$425M plant only with reasonable costs. Increase boil-up strongly at root/T to lift butane and all C5 into the intended outlets, and increase reflux on all three columns. Inspect purity and cost before adding C4 or heavy columns.

note: Use the proven root C5/C6 cut, make C5 blend in the light branch, and sharpen the C6-paraffin split enough to exceed 95%.
notebook:

Discard the unhelpful light column: T should instead reject C3/C4 overhead and leave a C5 blend bottom; B should separate C6 paraffins from naphthenes/heavies. Agent-48's 35/2/2 C6 split was only 86% paraffins, so use 60/5/2. Root is expensive (~$268M), but C5+C6 blend revenue is about $499M and this should give a valid positive starting point.

note: Raise both daughter boil-up ratios: the light branch needs a 95% C5 blend bottom, while the heavy branch must recover the C6 paraffins currently lost to its bottoms.

notebook:

If uneconomic, revert to the two-column R375 design and optimize its costs instead.

notebook:
